Google's desktop homepage now has a sidebar with your recent AI Mode chats.
You can reopen an old thread, start a new one or search past ones, right from google.com.
It is rolling out worldwide on desktop, gradually.

site_article.headline: Google adds an AI Mode chat history sidebar to its desktop homepage
site_article.dek: A collapsible panel on google.com lets people reopen recent AI Mode threads, start new ones and search older conversations.
site_article.summary: Google began rolling out a collapsible sidebar on its desktop homepage on November 19, 2026, that lists recent AI Mode conversations. The change is rolling out worldwide on desktop only, and Google has not said whether it will come to mobile.

paragraphs.text: Google has started adding a sidebar to its desktop homepage that keeps a list of recent AI Mode conversations, according to Digital Trends and Talk Android. Robby Stein, vice president of product for Google Search, announced the change on X on November 19, 2026, describing it as a collapsible sidebar for finding and returning to recent AI searches.

The sidebar is rolling out worldwide, but gradually. Digital Trends reported that it may take days or weeks to reach everyone. Neither report names specific countries or languages, and neither says whether a Google account sign in is required.
What the AI Mode sidebar shows

On google.com, the sidebar starts as a thin bar against the left edge of the page and stays collapsed until it is clicked, Talk Android reported. Digital Trends described the rail as holding a Google G icon for a new thread and a settings gear. Opening it reveals a panel with a New thread button, a tool to search older threads and a Recent list of past AI Mode conversations.

Choosing a past thread opens it in AI Mode with a box to keep the conversation going. Digital Trends said the panel also has a Notes section with an Add notebook option, while Talk Android described it as an option to connect a Gemini Notebook. The panel can be collapsed again to return to the plain homepage, and Talk Android noted that Google has not announced a setting to turn it off.
Why Google says it made the change

Stein said people are coming to Search with more questions that are not one and done, according to both outlets. Digital Trends reported that he said the sidebar made a big difference in testing for helping people make progress and keep exploring the web. Talk Android quoted him calling it a much simpler way to pick up where you left off.

The feature has been in testing for weeks. Both outlets pointed to a mid-October test, reported by Search Engine Roundtable, of a left side AI Mode panel on regular results pages. Talk Android also noted that Google tested three homepage buttons in August for creating images, asking about files and brainstorming. Digital Trends cited Google's figure from May that AI Mode had reached one billion monthly users.
For now the change only applies to desktop. Google has not said whether a similar panel will come to the Google app on Android and iPhone or to mobile browsers, Talk Android reported.

A history of past conversations on the left side of the screen is the standard layout of chatbot apps. Putting one on the Google homepage itself treats AI Mode as a place people return to over several sessions, not just a box for one quick answer, and it moves Google's most visited page closer to the apps it competes with.
The next thing to watch is whether Google brings the sidebar to its mobile app, where most searches happen, and whether it adds an option to hide it.
